content.text:
We need to resolve the March order from Winterfell. We have one unit: a knight (id 45). Supply is 1, currently Stark has supply=1, and currently armies? Let's see Stark units: winterfell (knight), castle-black (two knights), karhold (one knight), bay-of-ice (ship), the-narrow-sea (ship). Supply icons controlled: 1 (winterfell's supply icon =1). Supply track 1 allows army sizes: 2,2 (two armies max size 2 each). At present, they have armies: Are there any armies (2+ units)? In each area: winterfell 1 unit (not an army). castle-black 2 knights = army of size 2. karhold 1 knight (single). So they have one army size 2, okay. The ship at bay-of-ice is single, not army. So moving the knight from winterfell could leave winterfell empty; they have home castle, but they have no control token placed (but note: "No control token will be spent" and home symbol counts as control, so they can vacate without token). After moving, they'd have still the army at castle-black size 2 (max 2). If they also move the knight to somewhere else, they won't create new army unless they move to an area with another Stark unit.

Potential destinations: castle-black (controlled, no combat, castleAreasGainedIfCaptured 0, triggersCombat false). Here they'd have two knights together making army size 3? Wait castle-black currently has 2 knights (ids 2,28). Adding knight makes army size 3, which exceeds supply limit (max army size 2 at supply 1). That would be illegal because they'd exceed supply. However supply safe groups list for each destination likely ensures supply safe groups: the list shows supplySafeUnitIdGroupsWhenChosenAlone [[45]] for each destination, meaning moving unit 45 alone is supply safe. But that might consider after moving, the army size constraints: moving to castle-black would make army size 3 > max 2, so not safe. But the list shows safe group but maybe supply safe includes that you can move there only if you also move some units out? Actually they say supplySafeUnitIdGroupsWhenChosenAlone: groups of unit ids that can be moved alone safely. For castle-black they list [45]; meaning moving knight alone is supply safe. Possibly because the rule about army size doesn't apply when moving into area that already has units? But supply limit counts armies after movement; you would have a single army of size 3, which exceeds supply 1 (allowed sizes: 2,2). So maybe there is a rule that you can have army size up to 3? Wait supply track 1: table shows 0 -> 2,2 ; 1 -> 3,2 ; Actually supply=1 allows armies sizes 3 and 2 (one army size 3, another size 2). Wait earlier they gave table: supply 0: 2,2 ; 1: 3,2 ; 2: 3,2,2 ; 3: 3,2,2,2 ; etc. So at supply 1, allowed armies: one army max 3, another max 2. So army of size 3 is okay if they have only one army of size 3 and maybe another up to 2. They currently have army of size 2 (castle-black) plus maybe others. If they add knight to castle-black, they'd have army size 3, which is allowed (max 3). So okay.

Thus moving knight to castle-black is legal and would keep castle-black area unchanged (still Stark controlled, already castle). No new castle area gained.

Other destinations: flints-finger (castle level 1, controlled by greyjoy). No combat because triggersCombat false (since no enemy units there). Capturing would give castle area. Need to ensure supply safe: moving knight alone to flints-finger would create new army of size1 (single unit not army). That's fine. It would capture area (since no units there). Would the area have a castle, thus gives castle area.

Moat-cailin also castle level 1 greyjoy.

White-harbor also castle level 1, unoccupied.

The-stony-shore is land no castle.

Greywater-watch: castleLevel 0, but triggersCombat true (has enemy units). So moving there would start combat; need to check support. Probably not good.

We need to choose best move.

Stark's goal: increase castle count. Currently they have only winterfell (castle) and maybe some others? Winterfell is castle (1). So they have 1 castle area. Flints-finger, Moat Cailin, White Harbor are each castles that they could capture, gaining 3 more castle areas (total 4). That would be huge.

Supply wise moving the one knight to each of those (different moves?) only one destination can trigger combat; you can split the unit across multiple destinations? The group list only contains unit 45; you could move the knight to one destination only (since you have only one unit). You cannot move same unit to multiple places. So choose best capture.

Consider support: When moving to a castle area with no enemy units, no combat, you just occupy and gain control. No need support. So simply move knight to any of the three castles.

Which is best strategically? Greyjoy controls Flints-finger and Moat-cailin, both castles. Capturing them reduces Greyjoy's castle count (greyjoy has 4 castles currently). White Harbor currently uncontrolled (no controller). Capturing there would reduce overall unclaimed castle but not affect opponent directly.

Probably capturing Flints-finger might be better as it's adjacent to Greyjoy's units; also you may be able to support later. Let's see adjacency: Flints-finger neighbours: bay-of-ice (Stark ship), greywater-watch (Greyjoy), ironmans-bay, sunset-sea. So moving knight there would put Stark unit adjacent to Greyjoy's footmen/knights at Greywater-watch (enemy units). That could invite combat later maybe. But currently capture is safe.

Moat-cailin neighbours: greywater-watch, seagard, the-narrow-sea, the-twins, white-harbor, winterfell. So moving there would be adjacent to Greyjoy units as well.

White Harbor neighbours: moat-cailin, port-of-white-harbor, the-narrow-sea, the-shivering-sea, widows-watch, winterfell. Also adjacent to Greyjoy at moat-cailin but still.

All are similar. Perhaps choose Flints-finger as it's reachable via bay-of-ice (adjacent) but we are moving from winterfell directly; the action guidance shows reachable from Winterfell includes flints-finger (they are adjacent via bay-of-ice? Actually winterfell adjacency: flints-finger is listed as reachable, so okay.

Thus choose to move the knight (id 45) to flints-finger, capturing a castle.

We must ensure no combat: triggersCombat false.

Thus the moves list: one entry with destination regionId "flints-finger", unitIds [45].

We need JSON format expected by system. Likely they expect something like:

{
  "moves": [
    {"regionId":"flints-finger","unitIds":[45]}
  ]
}

But we need to look at schema used by earlier decisions. Not provided, but we can infer from other similar tasks. The final answer should be JSON matching expected format for resolve-single-march.

Probably format: {"movements":[{"regionId":"flints-finger","unitIds":[45]}]}

We can check earlier coding tasks; but not available. Might be simply {"unitMoves":[...]}.

We can look at actionGuidance constraints: "Move groups are processed in list order." So expects list of groups.

Possibly key "moves". Use that.

Thus final answer:

{
  "moves": [
    {
      "regionId": "flints-finger",
      "unitIds": [45]
    }
  ]
}

Let's output that.

moves.description: Destination groups and moving unit IDs. Unlisted units stay in the source. An empty list discards the order. Every group must be legal and fit Supply; an illegal final action is rejected without submitting the march.

actionOutputSchema.title: resolve_march_args
actionOutputSchema.description: You are resolving one of your March orders. Choose which units move and their destinations. Units you omit remain in the source area; you may split an army across destinations, and a single unit can march on its own. An empty moves list removes this March order without moving anyone. Only one destination may start combat. Use the reachable destinations in actionGuidance and keep the resulting armies within Supply. Leaving a control token costs one available power token and preserves control of the source when you legally vacate it. Compare castles gained and lost, and count support around the destination battlefield before choosing an attack. Before attacking another army, use check_neighbours on that battlefield to verify the supporting areas. Your final answer resolves this one order; another remaining order is a later decision.
